answer: Proof-of-replication leases tie rewards to distinct stored encodings. An opal survey's horizon images and signal traces are encoded with each lease's unique salt. The verifier challenges unpredictable blocks under a response deadline and pays per proved byte, never per account. N full leases require N encodings held on disk, costing storage and bandwidth. This assumes the encoding resists deduplication and cannot be regenerated within the deadline; enough fast computation could weaken that storage bound.
